analysis.title: Flows & Liquidity: Retail investors continue to buy the dip
key_insights: Retail investors remain bullish on equities and keep buying the dip in November after strong equity fund buying in October. Equity ETF buying rose to $20bn per day last week and reached $30bn on Monday Nov 9.

Leveraged equity ETF inflows were close to $5bn on Nov 5-6, equal to about $15bn of capital after leverage. Inverse equity ETFs saw about $5bn of outflows over the past week, an added bullish flow impulse.
The stock of leveraged equity ETFs as a % of underlying market cap unwound close to 90% of its April-June increase by Nov 5, and recent inflows follow that reduction.

Retail call option buying (small-lot customers on single stocks) has retrenched further in recent weeks after a sharp fall from the early June peak, which in principle leaves room for the retail impulse to intensify.

Retail support is described as essential to stabilize the AI trade in November. Stability in November could let hedge funds rebuild AI exposure from end-November, helping a year-end rally. This follows a 'performance bloodbath' and severe hedge fund de-risking in October.
Hedge fund de-risking shows in QQQ short interest at its highest since 2023, the Nasdaq futures positioning proxy, and CTA/momentum proxies.

Equity strategy (Lakos-Bujas, Nov 7) describes an extreme reversal of the AI trade: MTUM relative to SPY fell by Nov 5 to its lowest since August 2024, unwinding more than two years of AI vs non-AI outperformance in a few months.
12-month forward PE multiples of AI subsectors (semis ex-memory, memory, hyperscalers, AI equipment/connectivity, AI utilities/power) are at their lowest since the AI trade began in 2023.

The Nov 5 drawdown was amplified by mechanical leveraged ETF rebalancing flows of about $45bn, partly offset by capital inflows into leveraged and unlevered equity ETFs, leaving net flow of -$6bn on the day.
CTA momentum z-scores fell about 0.6 standard deviations on Nov 5 for Nasdaq and on Nov 5-6 for Nikkei and MSCI Taiwan, suggesting momentum investors amplified the move.

L/S hedge funds had already cut exposure before Nov 5. HFRX Equity Hedge lost about 1.2% on Nov 5 vs a 2.1% cumulative drawdown from Oct 1 to Nov 4 and a 6.6% Nasdaq 100 drawdown, with rolling beta to Nasdaq averaging about 0.27. Equity market neutral (quant proxy) lost 0.2%.

Risk parity funds lost about 0.9% on Nov 5 vs about 0.4% for the benchmarks, pointing to some volatility-induced de-risking. The 20 largest balanced mutual funds lost about 2.1% vs a 4.4% S&P drawdown, so they do not appear to have de-risked significantly.

The 20 largest active global equity funds returned about -3.3% vs -3% for MSCI ACWI. Their beta rose from below 0.9 in early October to about 1.06 on Oct 28 and again Nov 5, consistent with some real money de-risking.
AI company CDS trading volumes rose sharply in Q3 and Q4 (Q4 estimated from SDR data scaled to DTCC). Q4 growth is driven mostly by Amazon, Oracle and Alphabet, with Oracle and Amazon dominant.

Oracle CDS volumes peaked in the week ending Oct 23 and have subsided, perhaps signaling calmer neocloud funding fears. Oracle's investor day two weeks ago and CoreWeave's better-than-expected earnings the night before helped calm fears.
CoreWeave CDS volumes remain a small fraction of Oracle's: CoreWeave is high yield with about $20bn of bonds, Oracle is investment grade with about $130bn of bonds.

Cross-asset vol monitor (as of Nov 9): 3m implied vol is 16% for S&P 500 (0.70x implied/realized), 51% for Brent, 22% for gold, 41% for CDX IG (1.51x) and 43% for CDX HY (1.68x). Credit and rates vol are rich vs realized.
Bitcoin market price is $74k vs a production cost of $95k per the monitor, and CME Bitcoin turnover is down 33% y/y.
earnings_insights: CoreWeave reported better-than-expected earnings on the night of Nov 10, per the report. No figures are given.
crypto_views: Bitcoin market price is $74k against an estimated production cost of $95k (Hayes 2018 cost-of-production approach).
CME Bitcoin turnover is down 33% y/y and CME Ethereum turnover is down 20% y/y (as of Sep-26).
risk_factors: Retail dip-buying may not be enough to stabilize the AI trade if hedge funds do not rebuild exposure from end-November.
Mechanical leveraged ETF rebalancing, risk parity vol targeting and CTA momentum signals can amplify drawdowns, as on Nov 5.
Neocloud funding fears, shown in Oracle and CoreWeave credit markets, could return.
Real money active funds' rising beta implies possible further de-risking.
charts_described: Figure 8 plots MTUM relative to SPY, which by Nov 5 fell to its lowest since August 2024.
Chart A37 states Bitcoin production cost at $95k vs market price at $74k.
vol_and_positioning: QQQ short interest rose to its highest level since 2023.
Leveraged equity ETF rebalancing flow reached about $45bn on Nov 5, with net equity fund flow of -$6bn that day after offsets.
Momentum z-scores for Nasdaq, Nikkei and MSCI Taiwan fell about 0.6 standard deviations around Nov 5-6.
HFRX Equity Hedge rolling 21-day beta to Nasdaq averaged about 0.27 recently, which implies hedge funds have lowered beta significantly.
3m ATM implied vol (Nov 9): S&P 500 16%, EuroSTOXX 16%, Nikkei 29%, MSCI EM 27%, gold 22%, Brent 51%, CDX IG 41%, CDX HY 43%.
Implied/realized vol ratios are above 1.4x for CDX IG (1.51x), CDX HY (1.68x), 10y Eur swaps (1.71x), USD/JPY (1.60x) and the BB commodity index (1.39x). S&P 500 is at 0.70x.
Retail small-lot call option buying remains far below its early June peak.
cross_bank_references: JPM equity strategy (Lakos-Bujas), 'Market Update, Anatomy of Momentum Crash, Leadership into 1Q27', Nov 7, is cited for the extreme reversal of the AI trade.

tension_points.bull_case: Retail dip-buying, leveraged ETF inflows, inverse ETF outflows and lower retail call buying leave room for stabilization in November. Hedge funds could rebuild AI exposure from end-November and help a year-end rally.
tension_points.bear_case: The AI trade has seen an extreme reversal: MTUM/SPY at its lowest since Aug 2024, AI sector forward PEs at lows since 2023, QQQ short interest at its highest since 2023, and mechanical flows amplified the Nov 5 selloff.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Retail support fading in November so hedge funds do not rebuild AI exposure from end-November.
